description: DistrictGenerator builds district energy scenarios from limited building and site information. RWTH Aachen University publishes the Python workflow to combine archetypes, stochastic occupancy, reduced-order thermal models, renewable generation and energy-system optimisation. Inputs include building type, construction year, retrofit condition and floor area. Users can change the location, weather reference year and profile resolution; the software does not provide one fixed historic district dataset. Outputs include demand and generation series, technology sizing, operating schedules and performance indicators. GitHub provides code, examples and an MIT licence, permitting free reuse. The README documents Pyomo optimisation, with Gurobi in the example configuration and HiGHS as an open alternative. Archetype defaults, building-stock assumptions and solver configuration limit interpretation for a particular neighbourhood. The tool supports early planning of heat pumps, photovoltaic systems, storage and district supply. Related record model-energyplus offers detailed building simulation at a different level; no direct interface was checked. No profiles or optimisation results were generated in this review.
